findings.claim: D-110 requires RestApp.create() to return an app assembled by the bootstrap module, but the bootstrap factory lookup (D-226), the missing-module failure (D-227) and the assembly of the TinyHttpd adapter plus GsonJsonCodec (D-228) are all section 5 (wave 5) items, and in the repo NaruServe/, NaruServe-tinyhttpd/ and NaruServe-gson/ contain only package-info.java. Wave 4 can add the static method but cannot make it return an assembled app or verify that, so D-110 as stated (and the 'default of RestApp.create() on the JVM' half of D-169) cannot be implemented or promoted in wave 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope D-110 in wave 4 to declaring `static RestApp create()` with the runtime lookup of D-226 and the D-227 missing-module exception (testable with no bootstrap on the classpath); move the assertion that it returns an assembled app, and the create() half of D-169, to wave 5 together with D-228 and D-402.

findings.claim: D-162 makes shutdown 'flush and close log writers', and D-180's rotating file logger needs a bounded queue and so a writer thread that I-015 requires gone after shutdown, but the Logger SPI of D-168 has only the six log methods and no flush/close. Nothing in the wave says how the core reaches a logger's writer, or whether it may close a user-supplied logger passed to app.logger(l) that another app shares.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide under D-181 a close/flush hook that does not change the six-method Logger: e.g. the core calls flush()/close() when the app logger implements java.io.Flushable/AutoCloseable (file logger implements AutoCloseable and stops its writer thread), and record in docs/api/logging.md that a custom logger set with app.logger(l) is closed by the app only if it implements AutoCloseable.

findings.claim: D-166 names a T44 test that sends a request on a keep-alive connection after STOPPING began and accepts TinyHttpd's idle close. Keep-alive connections and TinyHttpd's Connection.onServerStopping/closeIdle behaviour exist only with the TinyHttpd adapter (wave 5), and T44 is not in this wave's acceptance list (T35-T46 without T44). Wave 4 can only verify the dispatcher 503 + Connection: close through the in-memory adapter.
findings.suggested_fix: State in D-166 that wave 4 asserts the dispatcher 503 with Connection: close through the in-memory adapter and that the keep-alive socket case of the T44 test runs in wave 5 (TinyHttpd adapter) or wave 7 (T44).

findings.claim: D-142 requires req.service(T) to return the onStart instance 'for HTTP, WebSocket and SSE handlers alike (T41)', but app.ws and res.sse are wave 7; unlike D-117 and D-136 the wave does not defer the WebSocket/SSE assertions, so T41 cannot be fully satisfied in wave 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'with the WebSocket and SSE cases asserted in wave 7' to D-142, as D-117 does.

findings.claim: docs/api/middleware.md's status table lists 'server overload (queue full) 503' as a standard-error-JSON case, which contradicts D-134/D-400 (transport-level 503 is TinyHttpd's plain socket-level response that bypasses onError and the standard error JSON), and it omits the STOPPING 503 that D-134 adds. D-137 updates middleware.md but does not name this row, so the wave could leave a contradicting doc (I-008).
findings.suggested_fix: Have D-137's middleware.md update replace the overload row with 'request during STOPPING 503' and point transport-level 503 to docs/api/defaults.md (D-400).

findings.claim: docs/api/lifecycle.md says STARTING 'does not accept requests', while D-428 has the dispatcher hold requests that TinyHttpd accepts after bind on a start gate until RUNNING (or answer 503). The doc row becomes misleading once D-428 lands.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the STARTING row in lifecycle.md to say requests arriving after bind wait for RUNNING and get 503 + Connection: close if the start fails or is stopped.

findings.claim: D-167 is decided in wave 4, but no wave 4 adapter creates threads (the in-memory adapter is synchronous), and the HttpAdapter SPI's bind(host, port, handler) carries no daemon setting. TinyHttpd defaults Builder.daemon to true (acceptor and workers; the watchdog is always daemon), so if wave 4 chooses 'keep the JVM alive' (Express behaviour) only the wave 5 adapter can enforce it.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the decision in docs/api/app.md together with the note that the TinyHttpd adapter (wave 5) must call TinyHttpd.Builder.daemon(...) to match it, and carry that into wave 5.

findings.claim: D-129 requires onError to receive framework 415 errors, but no wave 4 API raises 415 (JSON bodies come in wave 5, forms and multipart in wave 6). Only 400 (malformed query) and 413 (BodyTooLargeException) have sources in the wave 3 code.
findings.suggested_fix: Test the 415 path in wave 4 through the D-130 status-carrying framework exception thrown from a handler, and assert the real 415 sources in waves 5 and 6.

findings.claim: The carried-from-wave-3 list gives 426 and 501 the standard error body, but D-134's status mapping names neither, so the code values D-137 must decide have no frozen mapping for these two statuses.
findings.suggested_fix: List 426 (WebSocket route without upgrade) and 501 (unsupported method) among the code values D-137 decides in middleware.md.

findings.claim: The last carried-from-earlier-waves bullet says the stop path uses the adapter deadline under 'D-154', but D-154 is the listen() order. The shutdown sequence is D-162 (and D-223 in wave 5). The other carried bullets match the merged wave 3 code: DefaultRestApp.freeze() and the ISE after freeze, the interim afterFailure/afterHandler rules, automatic() with Content-Length: 0, preCheck before any DefaultRequest, the malformed query 400 after the Request is built, and the HttpExchange lifetime javadoc.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'D-154 and the stop path' to 'D-162'.

findings.claim: NaruServe-filelog is API 21-targeted and documented as Android-supported, but its default directory ./logs resolves against the Android process working directory '/', which apps cannot write. With D-171 the logger fails silently on Android unless the caller passes a directory.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the ./logs default (object.md §10.3) but have D-181's logging.md update state that Android callers must pass an app directory such as Context.getFilesDir().
